summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86 down 0.28% for a second consecutive session of technology weakness, while the Dow held at 53,417.16 up 0.26%, cementing the defensive rotation that has now run two full days. The 10 year yield eased to 4.70 down 0.72% as Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond buyback program, which could exceed 4 billion dollars per operation and potentially draws on the Treasury General Account, kept a bid under bonds and pushed gold to 4,681.40 up 0.87%. The biggest single stock story was another wave down in the semiconductor and AI cloud cohort, with MU off 5.83%, NVDA off 2.91%, and quantum names IONQ and RGTI each falling roughly 8 to 9 percent, all ahead of NVDA earnings Wednesday. Bitcoin pulled back to 79,839.88 up 1.11%, giving back a small portion of yesterday's move above 80,000, while crude oil dropped to 83.33 down 1.98% as markets shrugged at US Iran sanctions. Canada and the US moved toward open trade war, with Ottawa announcing retaliatory tariffs after talks broke down and Trump threatening 50 percent levies on Canadian autos and parts, a development that matters directly to his Canadian equity exposure. The week's defining data hits Wednesday with Core PCE and preliminary GDP, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision.
